page: Microsoft Azure D48pls_v7 is an ARM-based virtual machine configured under Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs built on the arm64 architecture, paired with 96.0 GB of system memory. This configuration yields a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates without integrated local storage, requiring attached remote storage volumes, and supports Premium Storage configurations for persistent disk needs. No discrete GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned with this instance type.

The 1:2 memory-to-vCPU allocation positions the D48pls_v7 for computational tasks that do not demand extensive per-core RAM overhead. Relative to traditional general-purpose instances with 1:4 ratios, this configuration delivers higher core density per memory unit, providing cost-effective CPU scaling on ARM architecture. Because the instance contains zero local disk storage, workloads rely entirely on network-attached storage, which isolates compute scaling from local drive persistence.

This server type is suitable for compute-heavy ARM workloads that require broad multi-threaded scaling without excessive memory footprint. Typical use cases include continuous integration and build pipelines, code compilation, microservices hosting, distributed caching layers with moderate memory requirements, batch data processing, and scale-out web serving architectures.
